patch.value:
## Shape

    pm-changelog --exclude-tag changelog:ignore
    pm-changelog --exclude-tag changelog:ignore,upstream-tracker
    pm changelog generate --exclude-tag changelog:ignore

Default (flag absent) leaves output byte-identical.
Add --exclude-tag so tagged items can be omitted from generated changelogs

Duplicate check: searched all statuses for exclude ignore skip omit tag filter changelog; only --status/--statuses (status filter) and --limit/--since-version (section pruning) exist, and no item covers per-item exclusion. pm-changelog has no ignore convention: every closed item with a title lands in the changelog. Repos that track upstream/third-party issues, internal chores, duplicates or superseded work as pm items cannot keep those out of the user-facing changelog without deleting the item (losing the project-management context that is the whole point of tracking it). Add --exclude-tag <tags> (repeatable, CSV accepted) so a repo can standardize on e.g. changelog:ignore and keep tracker items in pm while excluding them from published release notes.

--exclude-tag <tags> omits items carrying any listed tag from all generation paths; Tag matching is case-insensitive and trims whitespace; Repeatable and comma-separated forms both accumulate; Exposed on the pm changelog extension subcommands and typed in the SDK options; --explain reports the excluded-by-tag count and sample ids
Fleet repos carry many upstream-tracking items (pm-cli issue mirrors) whose closure pollutes package release notes; the only workaround today is to never close them, which destroys tracking accuracy.

patch.value: Added --exclude-tag <tags> (SDK excludeTags): repeatable, CSV accepted, case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed, applied to every generation path and exposed on both extension subcommands. Hardened against malformed non-array tags after a CodeRabbit finding.
Items tracked in pm but not user-facing package changes (upstream issue mirrors, internal chores, superseded work) can be closed without polluting release notes.

Verified with real pm data: a changelog:ignore-tagged item is dropped from the CLI, extension and exporter paths while remaining fully intact in the tracker; --explain reports excluded_tag counts and sample ids.
Shipped in PR #92: --exclude-tag provides the ignore convention
